questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a muonic atom, a muon of mass of $200$ times of that of electron and same charge is bound to the proton. The wavelengths of its Balmer series are in the range of
questions.solution:
A muon is an unstable elementary particle of mass nearly $200{m}_{e}$ and charge $\pm e$.

Here, a negative muon is given bound to a proton.

So, $m = 200{m}_{e}$ and $M = 1836{m}_{e}$

(as mass of a proton is $1836$ times of mass of electron)

So, reduced mass of system,

$m^{'} = \dfrac{mM}{m + M} = \dfrac{200{m}_{e} \times 1836{m}_{e}}{200{m}_{e} + 1836{m}_{e}} \approx 180{m}_{e}$

As mass of muon is comparable to mass of proton, we have to take account of motion of nucleus. That's way we are calculating reduced mass.

Now, as energy of an electron in $nth$ orbit is of $H$-atom,

${E}_{n} = \dfrac{me^{4}}{8{ε}_{0}^{2}h^{2}n^{2}}$

So, energy of a muon of muonic atom is

${E}_n^{'} = \dfrac{m^{'}e^{4}}{8{ε}_{0}^{2}h^{2}n^{2}} ⇒ {E}_n^{'} = 180{E}_{n}$

Now, considering a Balmer transition, $n = 3$ to $n = 2$.

$∴ \Delta E^{'} = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$

or $\Delta E^{'} = {E}_{n = 3}^{'} - {E}_{n = 2}^{'} = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$

$⇒ 180\left({E}_{n = 3} - {E}_{n = 2}\right) = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$

$⇒ 180\left(\dfrac{- 13. 6}{32} - \dfrac{- 13. 6}{22}\right) = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$

$⇒ 180 \times 189eV = \dfrac{1240\left(eV \cdot nm\right)}{\lambda\left(nm\right)}$

$⇒ \lambda\left(nm\right) = 3. 6nm$

This emitted radiation is $X$-rays.

Note $X$-rays have a wavelength range of $0. 01nm$ to $10$ nm.

questions.q:
The emission series of hydrogen atom is given by

$\frac{1}{\lambda}=$R$\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right)$where $R$ is the Rydberg constant. For a transition from $\mathrm{n}_{2} to \mathrm{n}_{1}$, the relative change $\Delta \lambda / \lambda$ in the emission wavelength if hydrogen is replaced by deuterium (assume that the mass of proton and neutron are the same and approximately 2000 times larger than that of electrons) is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrme^{4}}{8 \varepsilon_{0}^{2} \mathrm{ch}^{3}}$where $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}=$ mass of electron
When we consider mass of nucleus also then we replace $\mathrm{m} with $reduced mass

\mu=$\frac{m_{e} m}{m_{e}+m}$where $\mathrm{m}=mass of $nucleus
In case of hydrogen atom

\mu_{1}=$\frac{\left(\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)\left(2000 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}+(2000) \mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}}=\frac{2000}{2001} \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}In case of $deuterium

\mu_{2}=$\frac{\left(\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)\left(4000 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}+(4000) \mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}}=\frac{4000}{4001} \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}$Hence,

$\begin{aligned}\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}}$&=$\frac{\mathrm{R}_{2}}{\mathrm{R}_{1}}=\frac{\mu_{2}}{\mu_{1}}$\\
&=$\left(\frac{4000 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}}{4001}\right) \frac{(2001)}{\left(2000 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}\right)}$\\
&=$\frac{4002}{4001}$\\
\Rightarrow $\frac{\lambda_{2}}{}^{-\lambda_{1}}{\lambda_{1}}=$& $\frac{1}{4001}$\\
\therefore \quad $\frac{\Delta \lambda}{\lambda_{1}} \times$100 &=$\frac{1}{4001} \times$100 \\
&=0.025 \%
\end{aligned}

questions.q: The Hitomi satellite recently observed the Lyman alpha emission line (n = 2$ to $n = 1$) of hydrogen-like iron ion (atomic number of iron is 26$) from the Perseus galaxy cluster. The wavelength of the line is closest to
questions.solution:
Using Balmer's formula, wavelength $\lambda$ of emission from ion is

$\dfrac{1}{λ} = RZ^{2} \left(1{n}_f^{2} - 1{n}_i^{2}\right)$

Here, Rydberg constant, $R = 109 \times {10}^{7}m^{- 1}$

Atomic number of iron, $Z = 26$

${n}_{i} = 2, {n}_{f} = 1$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{λ} =109 \times {10}^{7} \times \left(26\right){}^{2} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{22}\right)$

$⇒ \lambda = 18 \times {10}^{- 10}\overset{o}{A}$

or $\lambda \approx2\overset{o}{A}$

questions.q: Instead of angular momentum quantization a sudent posits that energy is quantized as $E = - {E}_{0} / n  \left({E}_{0}> 0\right)$ and $n is a positive integer. Which of the following options is correct?$
options: The radius of the electron orbit is $r ∝ \sqrt{n}$
The speed of the electron is $v ∝ \sqrt{n}$
The angular speed of the electron is $\omega ∝ 1 / n$
The angular momentum of the electron is $∝ \sqrt{n}$
questions.solution:
${F}_{e} = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} ⇒ \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r} = \dfrac{k ( Ze ) ( e )}{r2}$
$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \dfrac{KZe^{2}}{2r} \ldots \left(i\right)$ (Kinetic energy)

Potential energy $= \dfrac{K{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{r} = \dfrac{K ( Ze ) ( - e )}{r} \ldots\left(ii\right)$

Total energy $= KE + PE = - \dfrac{KZe^{2}}{2r} = - \dfrac{E0}{n}$
$∴ r ∝ n$
As kinetic energy $= \dfrac{KZe^{2}}{2r} ⇒ KE ∝ \dfrac{1}{n}$
or $v^{2} ∝ \dfrac{1}{n} ⇒ v^{2} ∝ \dfrac{1}{n}$
$L = mvr$
$L ∝ vr$

$L ∝ \dfrac{1}{n} ( n ) ∝ \sqrt{n}$
$⇒ L ∝ \sqrt{n}$
